data.gist: Authors conclude the findings support the idea that preserving the native marrow microenvironment and cell–matrix integrity, not just cell number, drives MSC therapeutic performance.
data.plain: Summing up, the authors argue their results back the concept that keeping the bone marrow's natural extracellular matrix and stromal structure intact improves outcomes: micronized bone marrow gave better anti-inflammatory effects, less movement-evoked pain, and better cartilage preservation than BMAC in a rat post-traumatic osteoarthritis model. They frame this as evidence that MSC effectiveness depends on cell–matrix interactions rather than cell count alone, and that niche-preserving approaches may advance orthobiologic therapies.
